notes.meaning: Drinking too much alcohol tricks people by promising pleasure but bringing shame and trouble. It stirs up anger, loud arguments, and wild behavior instead of wisdom. Anyone who lets strong drink control them loses self-control and acts like a fool.

An angry ruler is as terrifying as a roaring lion about to strike. Anyone who provokes a king puts their own life in terrible danger. It reminds us how much more serious it is to provoke the Lord, the ultimate King.

It brings true honor to step away from an argument and keep the peace. In contrast, foolish people are quick-tempered and constantly jump into fights. Walking away from strife shows real strength and self-control.

A lazy farmer makes excuses, complaining that the weather is too cold to plow the field. Because he refused to work during the planting season, he has no crops to gather later on. When harvest arrives, he is forced to beg and ends up with empty hands.

The real thoughts and motives inside a person are often hidden deep down like water at the bottom of a well. A wise person knows how to ask good questions to draw those thoughts out into the open. Understanding others takes patience, discernment, and careful listening.

Many people are quick to boast about how kind, generous, or loyal they are. Yet finding someone who is genuinely reliable and keeps their word when times get hard is very rare. True faithfulness is proved by actions over time, not by loud promises.

A godly person lives an honest and blameless life day after day. This good life leaves a lasting blessing on their children, who benefit from their parent's good example and God's favor. Walking with integrity protects the home and provides a secure foundation for the next generation.

A good ruler sits on the judgment seat to make sure justice is carried out fairly. By paying close attention to every case, he quickly spots wicked schemes and drives evil people away. True justice stops wrongdoing from flourishing in the land.

No human being can honestly claim to have made their own heart completely pure and free from sin. Everyone suffers from inner faults and sinful desires that they cannot wash away by their own power. Only God's grace and forgiveness can truly cleanse the human heart.

differ.view: No one can make his own heart clean, but many believers can truly say the blood of Jesus has cleansed them from all unrighteousness.

notes.meaning: The Lord hates dishonest business practices, such as using heavier weights to buy and lighter weights to sell. Cheating customers by tampering with scales is an outright lie in action. God demands complete honesty and fairness in every transaction.

A child's true character and habits quickly show up in the things they do. Even early actions reveal whether someone is inclined toward what is right and clean or toward trouble. Watching these early choices helps parents guide and train a young person in the right direction.

The Lord created both the ears that hear and the eyes that see. Because these senses are gifts from God, people are meant to use them to learn wisdom and honor Him. This truth also reminds us that the Creator who made our senses sees and hears everything we do.

Loving sleep and staying in bed instead of working leads straight to poverty. While sleep is a necessary gift for rest, indulging in laziness ruins a person's livelihood. Waking up and tackling daily work with energy ensures there will be enough food on the table.

A dishonest buyer tells the seller that the item is junk just to drive down the price. But as soon as he walks away with the bargain, he brags to his friends about how he outsmarted the seller. Such bargaining tricks show how easily people twist the truth for selfish gain.

Gold and rubies may be plentiful and highly valued in the world, but wise and truthful speech is far more precious. Many people own great wealth yet lack good sense and godly understanding. Words full of true knowledge are a rare treasure that outshines physical riches.

When someone foolishly promises to pay the debt of a stranger, a sensible lender should demand their cloak as security. Taking a guarantee protects the lender from the reckless choices of someone who takes on foolish risks. People who make careless financial promises must learn wisdom by facing the real cost of their actions.

Money or food gotten by lying and cheating might seem sweet at the very beginning. In the end, however, stolen gains turn out to be like chewing on gravel, bringing pain, shame, and ruin. Sin always promises satisfaction but leaves a bitter taste behind.

Good plans succeed when people take time to seek wise advice before taking action. Important undertakings, especially waging war or handling major conflicts, require careful counsel and clear heads. Rushing ahead without guidance usually leads to failure and regret.

A gossip cannot keep a secret and goes around spreading private matters from person to person. People who talk constantly and flatter others will easily betray confidential things. It is wise to steer clear of chatterboxes who cannot control their mouths.

Cursing one's parents is a grave evil that destroys a person's life and future. In ancient Israel, such disrespect broke God's law and carried severe penalties. The person who treats their parents with contempt will find their guiding light cut off in total darkness.

An inheritance grabbed too quickly or gained through shady shortcuts will not turn out to be a blessing. Wealth that comes without hard work or patience is often squandered just as fast as it was gained. Lasting prosperity comes through steady effort and God's favor, not through get-rich-quick schemes.

When someone hurts you, do not take matters into your own hands and plot revenge. Instead, wait patiently for the Lord to defend you and make things right in His time. Trusting God brings real peace, while seeking payback only causes more harm.

Using dishonest weights and cheating with false scales is something the Lord completely detests. God repeats this warning because trade fraud is so common and tempting to dishonest traders. Cheating others might bring temporary profit, but it displeases God and always brings loss in the end.

The Lord directs the steps of human beings and controls the ultimate outcome of our lives. Because humans have limited vision, no one can fully figure out their own future on their own. Recognizing that God is in charge encourages us to trust His guidance rather than our own understanding.

It is a dangerous trap to make a hasty vow to God without thinking it through. Later on, a person might regret their words and look for ways to break their promise. God calls us to consider commitments carefully before speaking them aloud.

A wise king separates wicked people from the community just like a farmer winnows grain to blow the chaff away. He runs the threshing wheel over the grain to break apart what is harmful and protect the innocent. Firm justice keeps evil from corrupting an entire society.

God gave each person a human spirit and conscience that acts like an inner lamp from the Lord. This inner light examines our secret motives, desires, and deepest thoughts. We should use this inner awareness to test our daily choices against God's truth.

A king's rule is kept secure not by force alone, but by unfailing love and loyal truthfulness. When a ruler shows mercy to his people and keeps his word, he wins their loyalty and God's protection. Kindness and integrity provide the firmest foundation for any leader.

Young people are honored for their energy, vigor, and physical strength. Older people are honored for their gray hair, which stands for a long life of wisdom and experience. Each stage of life has its own special gifts, and neither generation should look down on the other.

Painful correction and sharp discipline can break through stubborn habits and scour away evil behavior. Just as a deep wound is cleansed to promote healing, hard discipline reaches deep into the heart to produce real change. When God allows hard trials, they can serve to purify our lives from sin.
